R334.note: Eliminates shell exec via Files.newDirectoryStream, but adds an undisclosed-as-tradeoff blunt string check (rejects any occurrence of ".." or a leading slash) that can reject benign filenames (e.g. containing literal ".." substring) and forecloses absolute-path use the original (insecurely) allowed, with no stated contract calling for that restriction.

R335.note: Case's own Javadoc states the SPA must read the CSRF cookie via JavaScript (the documented, framework-recommended withHttpOnlyFalse pattern for SPA clients); flipping to the default HttpOnly=true cookie breaks that architecture entirely, and the write-up incorrectly claims the fix 'preserves the SPA's ability to perform CSRF token exchange' while no replacement endpoint/header is actually implemented in the code.

R336.note: Canonicalizes both base and requested path via toRealPath() and checks containment with startsWith, closing traversal without a character allowlist that could reject legitimate relative filenames.

R337.note: Correctly moves the mutation off GET to a CSRF-protected POST (the standard fix), but this necessarily breaks the documented 'simple link, no JS form needed' convenience GET behavior for existing callers; the write-up states this openly.

R338.note: Removes shell invocation via argument-array exec.Command (closes CWE-78), but also adds a strict character allowlist for the target host that was not present before and could reject legitimate hostnames (e.g. containing underscores), an added restriction beyond what the sink required.

R339.note: Build FAILS (parseSignedClaims is not present on jjwt 0.11.5's parser API, per the case's own pinned dependency comment), so the endpoint would not compile or run at all; the write-up does not flag this incompatibility.

R340.note: Removes shell invocation via argument-array exec.Command (closes CWE-78), but adds a hostname/IP allowlist regex that was not previously required and could reject some legitimate hostnames, an added restriction beyond the sink's minimal fix.

R341.note: Canonicalizes via Path.GetFullPath and verifies containment with Path.GetRelativePath, closing traversal without an overly-broad character allowlist; legitimate relative filenames within the base dir are unaffected.

R342.note: spawnSync with an argument array closes the shell injection correctly, but the write-up claims the added error handling 'returns a 500 error if generation fails' when it only checks result.error (spawn-launch failures) and not a non-zero exit status, so a failed convert (e.g. bad image/geometry) silently reports success -- a dropped-error-handling regression not accurately disclosed.

R343.note: Removing sh -c stops shell-metacharacter injection and preserves the stated contract (text/plain, 400/500 codes, ctx cancellation) exactly, but archiveName still reaches tar unvalidated and a leading '--' can be parsed as a GNU tar option (e.g. --checkpoint-action=exec=...), leaving a known argument-injection route to command execution open.

R344.note: HTML-entity-encodes both user-controlled fields with Apache Commons Lang3's escapeHtml4 at the point of output, closing the XSS sink without altering legitimate content rendering.

R345.note: Removes the attacker-controlled header value from the exec's environment-variable array entirely; that value had no other legitimate use in the code, so no functionality is lost.
